questions.question: What categories of bugs do AI code review tools consistently miss?
questions.answer_summary: Race conditions, security/authorization flaws, breaking API changes, and business-logic/intent errors are the recurring miss categories, per multiple benchmark studies.

questions.question: How good are AI code review tools at catching real bugs, quantitatively?
questions.answer_summary: A benchmark of 67 real production bugs found the best tool caught only 49% recall (F1 up to 47.2%), with Claude at 42.8% and Copilot at 22.6%; a larger 200k+ PR study found 50-60% field effectiveness.

questions.question: Why do static-analysis-style AI reviewers plateau around 50-60% detection?
questions.answer_summary: NIST SATE evaluations show static analysis tools plateau at 50-60% for security vulnerabilities, and a 2024 ISSTA study found 22% of vulnerable commits went entirely undetected across five tools.

questions.question: Is it risky to have the same AI model both write and review code?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — when the generating and reviewing model share the same training, they can carry the same blind spots into both jobs, creating confirmation bias at scale rather than independent verification.

questions.question: Does AI code review change what humans actually review?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — commenters and researchers note an AI reviewer changes what the human reviews, not whether the human reviews, and can create 'automation complacency' where a 50% catch rate gets trusted like a 90% one.

questions.question: What tools are teams using for human code review of AI-assisted code?
questions.answer_summary: An Ask HN thread surfaces a mix of AI reviewer add-ons (CodeRabbit-style bots) plus manual review discipline; commenters are split on whether dedicated tools add value over prompting a general model directly.

questions.question: Why does AI code review generate so much noise (false positives)?
questions.answer_summary: Commenters report AI reviewers deliver many speculative/nitpick comments alongside real findings, making it hard to separate signal from noise, and results can be non-deterministic across runs.

questions.question: Can AI code review understand architectural or business context?
questions.answer_summary: No — AI reviewers act mainly as an 'advanced linter,' missing duplicate code, cross-module coupling, and separation-of-concerns issues that require broader system/business knowledge.

questions.question: Does AI-generated code lead to more production incidents despite passing review?
questions.answer_summary: A survey of 105 engineering leaders found 61% shipped a production incident originating from AI-generated code within 90 days, even after it passed review and unit tests.

questions.question: Do AI reviewers detect hallucinated or non-existent APIs?
questions.answer_summary: AI review commonly fails to flag syntactically plausible but invalid code referencing functions or libraries that don't actually exist.

questions.question: How does human reviewer performance compare to AI on large diffs?
questions.answer_summary: Human reviewers also miss logic errors in large diffs, with detection degrading sharply past ~400 lines, meaning AI weaknesses aren't uniquely worse than human ones in every dimension.

questions.question: What is a 'design flaw' or 'intent violation' that AI review can't catch?
questions.answer_summary: Code that is syntactically correct and passes tests but solves the wrong problem — e.g., a bus-tracking app producing correct-looking but functionally wrong output, or Google's Gson null-key bug persisting through years of review.
